component.name: ScreenCap Docs
component.summary: Turn screen recordings into step-by-step screenshot documentation

description.p: ScreenCap Docs (formerly Screencap Documentation Tool) finds every step in a screen recording with FFmpeg scene detection and saves a screenshot of each one: a free Steps Recorder replacement that also runs on Linux. Built with system administrators in mind, and useful for anyone who writes how-to guides.

ul.li: A built-in recorder that notes your clicks: each step gets a red ring and a first-draft caption such as Click "Next"
Presets for installers, the desktop, web consoles, terminals, remote desktops, and more
Review the steps: reorder, delete, crop, and write a caption for each one
Arrows, numbered markers, text labels, a zoomed inset, and animated GIF clips
Blur passwords, keys, and addresses automatically, with an unblurred copy kept
Export to HTML, Word, PDF, or PowerPoint, with your logo and alt text on every picture
Light and dark themes; everything runs locally, with no telemetry

screenshot.caption: Each step with its screenshot, the click marked, secrets blurred, and a first-draft caption
Recording the screen with the built-in recorder
Arrows, numbered markers, and text labels on a screenshot
The finished document, exported as HTML
The steps as a PowerPoint presentation, one slide per step

description.p: Bug fixes: a recording no longer stops when a Windows administrator prompt appears, the last screenshot of a recording whose sound runs longer than its picture works, and the Windows file details show the copyright once.
ScreenCap Docs is now published by ILHS Software, LLC. The app, its MIT license, and your settings stay the same.
The Windows setup can add the screencap command to the PATH, and every release file now has a build provenance record.
Security and privacy fixes: characters typed with AltGr or Option are never noted as shortcuts, administrators can switch off noting keys, and captions in Word exports are shown exactly as typed.
Screencap Documentation Tool is now called ScreenCap Docs. Settings, folders, and commands are unchanged.
The Windows installer updates an installed copy without asking the install mode again.
Update Now in the update window installs new versions of the Windows build in one click; other installs get the command to copy.
About three times faster processing on multi-core PCs, and fixes for OCR stalls and unsaved edits.
Export to PowerPoint: one slide per step, with narration in the speaker notes.
Better first-draft captions from clicks, and screenshots in the software center listing.
Snap Store fix: the snap asks for audio playback together with the microphone.
A built-in screen recorder that notes clicks and keys, for click rings and first-draft captions.
Animated GIF clips of single steps.
Alt text on every screenshot in steps.md and exported documents.
Company logo and Word template for exported documents.
Zoomed inset that shows small changes up close.
Annotations: draw arrows, numbered markers, and text labels on screenshots.
Windows installer summary fixes (no Linux changes).
ARM support: a 64-bit ARM snap, and the package tested on 64-bit and 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS.
Windows installer wording and layout fixes (no Linux changes).
The Windows installer can set the recordings and output folders; the snap is published to the Snap Store.
New winget package ID for Windows (no Linux changes).
The Windows installer updates an installed copy in place (no Linux changes).
Themed menu bar, a clearer About window and Advanced Settings window, and update status in the status bar.
Homebrew formula for macOS.
Packages for Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, openSUSE, Arch Linux, and the Snap Store.
